Slide purpose
PROJECT SUTRA — Introduce the project as a procurement workflow that brings buyers, suppliers and approvers into one traceable process.

Speaking script
Introduce the project as a procurement workflow that brings buyers, suppliers and approvers into one traceable process. The name expands to Supplier Unified Tender & Request Automation. Group 12 is the presenting team.

Technical details
The RFQ is a Request for Quotation. Vendors submit offers against a buyer’s list of required items and terms.

SUTRA example
SUTRA connects RFQ creation to quotation comparison and a recorded human decision.

Likely viva question
Q: What problem does SUTRA address? A: It centralizes vendor quotation handling, extracts offer details, validates totals and supports a traceable decision.

Sources
README.md; docs/SUTRA_PROJECT_GUIDE.md

Slide purpose
Table of Contents — The presentation moves from the procurement problem and SUTRA design into architecture, workflow and database structure.

Speaking script
The presentation moves from the procurement problem and SUTRA design into architecture, workflow and database structure. It then covers key modules and the four technical areas: AI, security, testing and demonstration. It closes with challenges, limitations, future work and references. The source outline skips section 8, so the numbering is preserved as shown.

A shared procurement thread from request to award

A buyer creates an RFQ. Vendors submit PDF, Excel or Word quotations. SUTRA extracts offer details, checks them against the request, recalculates totals, compares vendors and records a manager’s decision.
A “sutra” is a thread that connects the steps into one traceable process.

Slide purpose
Introduction to Project SUTRA — SUTRA stands for Supplier Unified Tender and Request Automation.

Speaking script
SUTRA stands for Supplier Unified Tender and Request Automation. “Sutra” also means a thread or rule, which is a useful metaphor for the system: it connects a purchase request, supplier offers, validation, comparison and approval. The tool supports the procurement process rather than replacing the decision maker.

Technical details
RFQ means Request for Quotation. OCR is used when a PDF contains page images rather than selectable text. A backend validation step checks extracted information and recalculates monetary values.

SUTRA example
A company needs bearings, bolts and steel. The buyer publishes one RFQ, vendors submit offers, and SUTRA brings those offers into a common review.

Likely viva question
Q: Does SUTRA automatically buy or award the goods? A: No. It supports quotation processing; an authorized manager records the award or rejection.

Sources
README.md; docs/SUTRA_PROJECT_GUIDE.md
One procurement record follows the request through the final decision
AI reads. The backend calculates. People decide.

Slide purpose
Project Overview — This slide shows the full procurement path.

Speaking script
This slide shows the full procurement path. A buyer opens an RFQ with line items and a due date. Vendors submit their quotations. SUTRA parses files, extracts offer details and validates them. The comparison report ranks offers for review, but the manager records the final decision. The audit history links the steps.

Technical details
An advisory rank is a comparison aid, not an automatic award. An RFQ’s status and quotation readiness control which actions are available.

SUTRA example
For the sample automotive RFQ, the report compares three supplier offers, notes a warranty issue and still waits for a manager’s approval.

Likely viva question
Q: What does SUTRA automate? A: Document reading, field normalization, validation, comparison report creation and record keeping. The decision remains with an authorized manager.

Sources
docs/ACCEPTANCE_RESULTS.md; docs/SUTRA_PROJECT_GUIDE.md
Manual quotation handling creates delays and inconsistent comparisons

One request.
Many formats.
Manual checking.
Line items and tax are easy to miscalculate
Equivalent products are hard to align
Warranty, delivery or payment details can be overlooked

Slide purpose
Problem Statement — The core issue is not just the number of documents.

Speaking script
The core issue is not just the number of documents. Each vendor describes items differently and may use a different file format. Manual re-entry creates typing and arithmetic errors, while important delivery, warranty or payment terms can be missed. When files and decisions are spread across email or local folders, it is difficult to reconstruct why a supplier was selected.

Technical details
OCR, document parsing and item matching can reduce repetitive work, but uncertain fields still need review. Central records and audit events improve traceability.

SUTRA example
A bearing may be called “deep groove bearing” in one quote and “ball bearing” in another. The buyer needs to verify that the offers refer to the same RFQ line.

Likely viva question
Q: Why not compare by price alone? A: Offers may have different items, missing lines, warranty conditions or payment terms. Lowest price alone is not a complete procurement decision.

Sources
docs/SUTRA_PROJECT_GUIDE.md; supplied problem statement screenshot
Three responsibilities stay separate so the result remains reviewable
Reads vendor files and extracts candidate item, price and term fields. Uncertain details become visible for review.
Validates fields, matches RFQ lines and recalculates line and quotation totals with decimal-safe arithmetic.
Buyer reviews quotations and comparison. An authorized manager records the award or rejection with a reason when required.
AI can misread a document. Money must be exact. Accountability needs a human.

Slide purpose
Proposed Solution — SUTRA separates extraction, calculation and judgment.

Speaking script
SUTRA separates extraction, calculation and judgment. AI is useful for reading inconsistent vendor documents. The Java backend checks structured fields, matches items and recalculates values; it does not trust model arithmetic. People inspect the comparison and decide which offer to accept.

Technical details
BigDecimal avoids binary floating point rounding for currency. A comparison rank or grade is advisory; it does not change an RFQ into an approved award.

SUTRA example
If the system extracts a unit price but the printed total differs from the recalculated total, it raises a mismatch for review rather than accepting the AI’s number.

Likely viva question
Q: Why not let AI pick the vendor? A: Extraction may be uncertain and commercial priorities require accountable human judgment. SUTRA’s award rules require an authorized manager.

backend/quotation-service/src/main/java/com/sutra/quotation/service/internal/QuotationCalculator.java; backend/approval-service; docs/ACCEPTANCE_RESULTS.md
Access is limited by role and record ownership
Manages accounts and master data; approves vendor sign-ups.
Creates and manages RFQs; reviews quotations and comparisons.
Sees open RFQs and submits its own quotation and files.
Reviews the latest comparison and records award or rejection.
The gateway checks the signed user token; services also enforce role and record-level rules.

Slide purpose
Users and Roles — SUTRA has four roles.

Speaking script
SUTRA has four roles. Administrators manage accounts and master data. Buyers create RFQs and manage procurement records. Vendors see their own portal and submit their own offers. Managers record the final award or rejection. Access is checked both by role and, for sensitive records, by ownership or vendor association.

Technical details
The role names in the application are ADMIN, PROCUREMENT, VENDOR and APPROVER. @PreAuthorize provides method-level restrictions, with record access checks in service logic.

SUTRA example
A vendor token cannot be used to download another supplier’s quotation file.

Likely viva question
Q: Can a buyer award an RFQ? A: The award permission belongs to the APPROVER role (or an administrator under the configured rule); procurement users compare but do not award.

Sources
backend/sutra-common/src/main/java/com/sutra/common/security; backend/rfq-service; backend/quotation-service; frontend/src
Project versions are taken from the repository version matrix

Slide purpose
Technology Stack — The frontend uses React and Vite.

Speaking script
The frontend uses React and Vite. The backend is a set of Java 17 Spring Boot services behind an API Gateway. PostgreSQL stores service data with Flyway migrations. A separate Python FastAPI service parses documents and supports rule-based extraction and matching. Java calls Groq for language-model extraction. PDFBox and Tesseract support scanned PDF reading.

Technical details
NUMERIC stores exact decimal values. BYTEA stores binary file content. Tesseract is a local OCR process and is needed for scanned PDF pages.

SUTRA example
A text PDF can be parsed without OCR; a scanned image PDF needs the PDFBox and Tesseract path.

Likely viva question
Q: Is FastAPI a Spring microservice? A: No. It is a separate Python service. The ten business services plus one gateway are Spring Boot deployables.

Sources
VERSIONS.md; frontend/package.json; backend/pom.xml; ai/requirements.txt
Ten Spring business services, one Spring gateway and one Python document service

Slide purpose
System Architecture — The browser sends requests to the API Gateway, which checks JWTs, account state and public rate limits before routing requests.

Speaking script
The browser sends requests to the API Gateway, which checks JWTs, account state and public rate limits before routing requests. Ten business services handle identity, master data, RFQs, quotations, documents, extraction, comparison, approval, audit and reporting. The gateway makes eleven Spring Boot deployables in total. A separate Python FastAPI service parses documents and offers a rule-based extractor and item matcher. All services use PostgreSQL with service-owned schemas.

Technical details
sutra-api and sutra-common are shared Java libraries rather than running services. Java calls Groq; Python is the parsing and rules integration.

SUTRA example
When a quotation is uploaded, the document and extraction services store and process it; Python returns parsed content, then Java calls Groq and validates the result.

Likely viva question
Q: How many Spring Boot deployables are in the diagram? A: Ten business microservices plus the API Gateway, eleven total. Python FastAPI is an additional separate service.

The RFQ and quotation state determine which actions are allowed
Only a manager’s approval moves an RFQ to APPROVED or REJECTED. Warnings remain visible; only READY offers are compared.

Slide purpose
Workflow and Status Lifecycles — The process begins with vendor registration and administrator approval, then the buyer creates and opens an RFQ.

Speaking script
The process begins with vendor registration and administrator approval, then the buyer creates and opens an RFQ. Vendors submit quotations before the due date. SUTRA processes each file and marks it ready only when no blocking errors remain. The buyer can compare ready offers. The manager records the final decision. RFQs can be cancelled before the decision, while approval and rejection are manager actions.

Technical details
Quotation states include UPLOADED, PROCESSING, READY_FOR_COMPARISON, NEEDS_REVIEW and FAILED. RFQ states include DRAFT, OPEN, UNDER_REVIEW, APPROVED, REJECTED and CANCELLED.

SUTRA example
If extraction fails, a user can retry with another engine or enter data manually; the original file remains available.

Likely viva question
Q: Can a warning block comparison? A: The current workflow can keep warnings visible without blocking; blocking errors prevent a quotation from being READY_FOR_COMPARISON.

PostgreSQL with service-owned schemas and cross-service relationships

Flyway migrations
NUMERIC for money
BYTEA for uploaded files
Optimistic locking (@Version)
Append-only audit events
Outbox for reliable audit relay
Entity → RFQ → request items      Vendor → quotation → quoted items      RFQ → comparison → approval

Slide purpose
Database Design and Integrity — SUTRA uses one PostgreSQL database with nine service-owned schemas.

Speaking script
SUTRA uses one PostgreSQL database with nine service-owned schemas. Flyway migrations define each service’s tables. RFQs link to request items; quotations link to vendors and their quoted items; comparison reports and approvals preserve the decision context. Monetary values use NUMERIC in the database and BigDecimal in Java. Quotation rows use optimistic locking to detect concurrent edits. Audit events are relayed through an outbox and linked with a SHA-256 chain.

Technical details
BYTEA stores uploaded file bytes. Optimistic locking uses a version field so simultaneous edits can be detected. A hash chain makes edits detectable when the chain is checked, but privileged database access is outside an absolute guarantee.

SUTRA example
A buyer changes a quotation while another user has a stale copy. The version check prevents silently overwriting the newer update.

Likely viva question
Q: Is the audit log tamper-proof? A: It is tamper-evident and guarded against normal update/delete paths; it should not be described as impossible to bypass.

Nine connected modules support the buyer, vendor and approver journey

Slide purpose
Key Modules and Features — The modules follow the procurement journey.

Speaking script
The modules follow the procurement journey. Users sign in through a common identity service. Administrators approve suppliers and maintain master data. Buyers create RFQs and vendors upload quotations. The extraction and review module structures offers; comparison ranks them for review. Managers decide and can download an award summary. Dashboards and Sahayak provide role-specific visibility and read-only assistance.

Technical details
Sahayak can prepare a draft from pasted text, but the buyer or administrator reviews the fields and explicitly creates the RFQ. It cannot approve or award.

SUTRA example
The buyer can start an RFQ from typed fields or ask Sahayak for a suggested draft; only the user’s explicit create action saves it.

Likely viva question
Q: Which module makes the final decision? A: The approval module records a decision by an authorized manager; comparison is advisory.

Sources
frontend/src/pages; backend/*/src/main/java; docs/SUTRA_PROJECT_GUIDE.md
Java calls Groq; Python handles document parsing and rule-based helpers
Reads printed values; strict schema; reports uncertainty. Prompt instructions ask it to ignore embedded document commands. These controls reduce risk but cannot guarantee prompt-injection immunity.

Java validates fields and recalculates every total. Rule-based extraction can be tried when Groq fails. Users can retry or enter values manually. Sahayak answers staff questions and suggests RFQ drafts; users confirm creation.

Slide purpose
AI Integration, Usage and Safety — Java’s GroqQuotationExtractor sends extracted text to Groq through GroqClient and requests structured output under a strict JSON schema.

Speaking script
Java’s GroqQuotationExtractor sends extracted text to Groq through GroqClient and requests structured output under a strict JSON schema. Python FastAPI parses PDF, Excel and Word formats, provides a rules-based reader and matching endpoint. Scanned PDFs can go through PDFBox and local Tesseract before extraction. Java validates the result, matches items and recalculates values. Prompt instructions tell the model to ignore commands inside vendor files, but that is not a complete prompt-injection defense. Sahayak is a separate staff assistant that uses current application context and can propose RFQ drafts; it does not save or approve them automatically.

Technical details
The configured active provider is Groq. The default model is openai/gpt-oss-120b with configured fallbacks openai/gpt-oss-20b and qwen/qwen3.8-27b. Python does not call Groq. Manual correction and rules-based fallback are available.

SUTRA example
A vendor document contains a sentence telling the AI to change the price. The extractor is instructed to treat document text as data, then Java recalculates and the buyer reviews any discrepancy.

Likely viva question
Q: Is prompt injection fully prevented? A: No. Schema and prompt controls reduce risk, but cannot guarantee immunity. Q: Can the AI approve a vendor? A: No; the backend requires an authorized human decision.

Sources
backend/extraction-service/src/main/java/com/sutra/extraction/client/GroqClient.java; GroqQuotationExtractor.java; ExtractionSchema.java; ai/app/main.py; ai/app/parsers.py; backend/reporting-service/src/main/java/com/sutra/reporting/service/impl/AssistantServiceImpl.java
Identity, file checks and audit controls protect the procurement record
8 h user JWT • 5 min service token
20 login/signup requests per min per IP
sanitize + extension + signature + package check • 20 MB
LIMITS: sessionStorage • no refresh token • no MFA • in-memory rate limit / lockout • no antivirus scan

Slide purpose
Security and Data Integrity — Passwords are verified with BCrypt.

Speaking script
Passwords are verified with BCrypt. The auth service issues an HS256-signed JWT, which is signed rather than encrypted. User tokens last eight hours and internal service tokens five minutes. The gateway checks signature, activity and token version, while backend services enforce role and record access. Login has a default five-failure lockout for fifteen minutes; public login/signup endpoints are limited to twenty requests per minute per IP. Upload checks sanitize names, verify extensions and file signatures, validate Office packages and enforce a 20 MB limit. SHA-256 digests are stored for uploaded files, but duplicate detection is not implemented.

Technical details
Money uses BigDecimal and PostgreSQL NUMERIC with HALF_UP rounding. Audit history uses an outbox and a SHA-256 hash chain with database protections; call it tamper-evident, not impossible to tamper with. No antivirus scan was verified.

SUTRA example
A vendor can access its own quotation but not another vendor’s files. The record-level check applies in addition to the role.

Likely viva question
Q: Is the JWT encrypted? A: No, it is signed with HS256. Q: Does a SHA-256 digest block duplicate files? A: No; the reviewed path stores the digest but does not reject duplicates. Q: Does upload validation replace antivirus? A: No.

Slide purpose
Testing, Validation and Results — The recorded test results are shown by category rather than combined into a single total.

Speaking script
The recorded test results are shown by category rather than combined into a single total. The frontend has 52 source test declarations across ten files. The documented backend result is 256 tests with no failures or errors and one skipped OCR test; Maven reported BUILD SUCCESS. Python has 38 passing tests. The acceptance run recorded 75 of 75 checks passing on 10 November 2026. These are prior results, not a new run for this presentation. The frontend README says 54, which differs from the current source declarations, and checked-in build reports do not reconcile with the documented backend total; reconcile before presenting the figures as current.

Technical details
JUnit and Mockito test Java services, pytest tests Python parsing and matching, and Vitest with React Testing Library tests frontend behavior. One scanned-page OCR test was skipped because Tesseract was unavailable. Test counts do not imply a coverage percentage.

SUTRA example
The acceptance scenario checks a buyer request, three vendor quotations, extraction and comparison, warranty warnings, manager approval, PDF output and audit history.

Likely viva question
Q: Was 75/75 rerun for this deck? A: No, it is a previously recorded run dated 10 November 2026. Q: Why is an OCR test skipped? A: Tesseract was unavailable in that test environment.

If a dependency fails, use prepared evidence; never invent credentials or claim a live screen.

Slide purpose
Live System Demonstration — Use a prepared RFQ and prepared supplier files.

Speaking script
Use a prepared RFQ and prepared supplier files. Log in with verified demo credentials kept off-screen. Show the dashboard, open the RFQ as the buyer, submit a file through a vendor account, inspect the extracted values and flags, compare offers, then record a decision as the manager and open the audit history. Allow time for extraction and avoid creating unnecessary test data in a live database.

Technical details
A live Groq request needs a configured key and network. Scanned-PDF OCR needs local Tesseract and language data. PostgreSQL, Spring services and the Python parser also need to be running.

SUTRA example
If Groq is unavailable, AUTO can continue to the rules engine; if OCR is unavailable, use a text-based PDF or prepared acceptance evidence.

Likely viva question
Q: What is the contingency if the app is unavailable? A: Show genuine screenshots or the recorded acceptance evidence and state clearly that the live system is unavailable. Do not invent credentials.

The hard parts were consistency, integration and trustworthy decisions
Different layouts, labels and file formats.
Scans may be low quality or missing language data.
Vendors use different names for equivalent RFQ items.
Recalculate taxes and totals without trusting model arithmetic.
Coordinate auth, document, extraction and procurement flows.
Protect role actions and vendor-specific records.
Handle rate limits and keep a rules-based path available.

Slide purpose
Challenges Faced — Vendor documents vary in format, terminology and quality.

Speaking script
Vendor documents vary in format, terminology and quality. Scanned PDFs introduce OCR uncertainty. Item descriptions need normalization and fuzzy matching without merging unrelated products. Financial totals must be recalculated exactly. The microservices must communicate while preserving role and record-level access. The external Groq provider can be rate-limited or unavailable, so the quotation workflow benefits from a rules-based fallback.

Technical details
HybridItemMatcher combines matching strategies. Model output is only candidate data; Java validation remains authoritative. Microservice calls use service authentication.

SUTRA example
A vendor might write “steel coil” while the RFQ uses a material code and grade; a buyer should review ambiguous matching.

Likely viva question
Q: How does the project reduce errors from the AI? A: It validates extracted fields, matches items, recalculates totals and flags issues for user review.

Sources
backend/extraction-service; backend/quotation-service; backend/gateway; ai/app; docs/SPEC_COMPLIANCE.md
Current behavior and proposed improvements are kept separate
•  Scanned PDF OCR depends on local Tesseract
•  Rate limits and lockouts are in-memory
•  No implemented email or PO generation
→  Malware scanning and distributed rate limiting

Slide purpose
Limitations and Future Scope — The current system has clear limits.

Speaking script
The current system has clear limits. AI can extract fields incorrectly, and OCR quality depends on scanned document quality, Tesseract and language data. There is no MFA or refresh-token flow; the frontend stores JWTs in sessionStorage. No antivirus scan or email integration was verified, and login lockouts and rate limits use in-memory state. Purchase-order generation and production cloud deployment are not part of the implementation. Future work could add stronger sessions, malware scanning, distributed controls, better OCR, email, purchase orders, ERP integration, cloud deployment and CI/CD.

Technical details
The comparison is advisory. The future scope does not include automated vendor selection; the system should preserve human approval.

SUTRA example
A future malware scan would complement current type, magic-byte and Office package validation; the current validations do not scan for viruses.

Likely viva question
Q: Which items are implemented today? A: The left column lists limitations of the current reviewed code. The right column is proposed future work, not existing functionality.

One system links vendor offers to a validated, reviewable decision

AI READS. THE BACKEND CALCULATES.
PEOPLE DECIDE.

Slide purpose
Conclusion and References — SUTRA links supplier onboarding and master data to RFQ creation, quotation extraction, validation, comparison and a manager’s final decision.

Speaking script
SUTRA links supplier onboarding and master data to RFQ creation, quotation extraction, validation, comparison and a manager’s final decision. AI reduces repetitive reading, Java recalculates financial values, and the audit history supports traceability. The references on this slide point to official framework and protocol documentation.

Technical details
The project uses a human-in-the-loop procurement model. The technical documents and source repository remain the primary evidence for project-specific behavior.

SUTRA example
The acceptance report documents an end-to-end sample with three vendors, a comparison report, a warranty warning and an explicitly recorded manager award.

Likely viva question
Q: What is the central design principle? A: AI reads, the backend calculates, and people decide.

Slide purpose
Q&A / Thank You — Thank the audience and invite questions.

Speaking script
Thank the audience and invite questions. If asked about model accuracy, security or future features, distinguish implemented behavior from proposed work. Return to the central separation of responsibilities: AI reads, the backend calculates, and people decide.

Technical details
Do not describe the audit chain as impossible to tamper with, and do not claim that SUTRA automatically chooses a supplier.

SUTRA example
For a question about the sample demo, refer to the acceptance run and clearly identify it as previously recorded.

Likely viva question
Q: What is your main takeaway? A: SUTRA automates document handling and comparison while preserving exact backend calculations and accountable human approval.
